ui.victoryScreen:
VICTORY.

The boss lies still on the stone, and the only sounds left are the torch and your own breathing. Its blood runs along the joints in the floor toward your boots.
ui.defeatScreen:
THE ENTIRE PARTY HAS FALLEN.

The torch rolls out of an open hand and burns on against the stone.
ui.endingCheckpointPrompt: The floor changes here, though none of you could say how. The stone underfoot is warm, and the corridor ahead has no doors.
ui.endingLeaveOnlyPrompt: There is no staying here and no going further. Only the way back up is still open.
ui.endingLeaveOnlyOption: [1] Turn back. There's nowhere else to go from here.
ui.endingStayOption: [1] Stay — and be part of what holds this floor together.
ui.endingLetGoOption: [2] Let go, together, all at once — however far down that leads.
ui.endingContinueOption: [3] Keep going, past the last place any of you would have turned back.
ui.endingStayScreen:
THE PARTY STAYS.

The way back up is where it always was, and a thin draft comes down it that smells of grass. No one climbs it. Packs come off and are left on the stone, straps still buckled; the torch burns down to a height it does not drop below again, and its light settles yellow and still on the walls. Much later, another party comes down this corridor. They do not know your names. Something in how they move through it is easier than it should be.
ui.endingLetGoScreen:
THE PARTY LETS GO.

None of you feel yourselves stop. The cold of the stone comes up through your knees, and then it is not cold. It comes gradually: the awareness that whatever is dreaming does not tell you apart from everything else it holds. The last clear thought any of you has, before the difference stops mattering, is of the sky above the entrance, wide and grey, the town you set out from with its wet roofs, the years before any of this. None of it was ever outside. It was a farther room of the same dream, dreamed calmly enough that no one standing in it needed to notice.
ui.endingLeaveAmbushedScreen:
AN UNKNOWN FATE.

The corridor you climbed through is gone. Where it should be there is only wall, smooth and seamless and cold to the palm, older than anything else on this floor. However you came down, it is not the way back up.

You start looking for another, running your hands along the joints, holding the torch close to every crack, and that's when you hear the breathing behind you, from more throats than one, close enough that they have been standing there the whole time you were looking at the wall.

Someone gets half a word out. The torch hits the floor and rolls, throwing their shapes huge across the stone, too many to count.
ui.founderDialogue:
The air in this chamber is warm and close, and smells of a sickroom. A shape larger than the doorway drifts in the dark ahead of you, more brain than body, ropes of nerve-thick tissue trailing beneath it where legs should be, reaching without ever quite touching the ground. Something wet drips from it and ticks on the stone. It has no face left to speak from. His voice comes anyway, from somewhere in the room.

"You made it further than any of them."
"I didn't come down here to build anything. I came down because everyone I was supposed to save was already gone, and I couldn't stop asking the ground to give them back."
"It never gave anyone back. It just... kept listening. So I kept asking. Eventually I stopped noticing I was still asking."

He is closer than he was. None of you saw him cross the distance.

"The others who followed me down, over the years — I taught them how to ask properly. That's all any of it ever was."
"I don't remember the last time I was only a person. I'm not sure there's a difference anymore, between what's still me and what's still just... dreaming."

Somewhere behind the walls, something takes a breath the room is too small to hold.

"You could have turned back, once. Now you can keep asking, the way I did, until there's nothing left to tell you apart from what you asked for."
ui.gatekeeperPaid: He doesn't count them. 'Then hear this. What's down there wants what you want, and it can wait longer than you can. The first thing that shines, leave it where it lies.' He presses two fingers to each of your brows and says something under his breath, in no tongue you know. 'That will follow you a little way. Not to the bottom.'
ui.gatekeeperBlessing: Blessed: {{stats}} for the next {{rooms}} {{rooms|room|rooms}} (rest rooms don't count).
ui.gatekeeperRefused: He laughs once, short, and steps aside from the cave mouth. 'Good luck, then.'
ui.gatekeeperMap: As you pass, he presses a square of hide into your hands. Lines are scratched into it, branching and meeting again. 'Someone left this with me. The ways are right. What waits in the rooms, it doesn't say.'
ui.gatekeeperMapTaken: The hide goes into your pack, folded along creases someone else made.
ui.endingLeaveEscapedScreen:
ESCAPED.

The corridor you climbed through is gone. Where it should be there is only wall, smooth and seamless and cold to the palm, older than anything else on this floor. However you came down, it is not the way back up.

A seam answers from further along the same dead-end wall, sealed shut, humming at a pitch none of you would have caught if you weren't already listening for anything. It isn't stone. Under your fingers it is warm and faintly soft, like old leather, and it has been failing for longer than any of you have been alive.

The shard fits. The seam parts along an edge worn smooth. On the other side is air: cold, wet with rain, smelling of grass and chimney smoke.

runner.notice0: The hood is the merchant's, cut smaller, and it smells of the same lamp oil. His pack is already open on the floor, every item with its mark turned toward you. "Late," he says, and bows exactly the way the merchant bows.
runner.notice1: A hooded figure is warming his hands at the fire, though the fire gives off no heat you can feel. His pack sits unstrapped beside him, the buckles worn bright by thumbs. "You took the long way," he says. "Sit, if you like. I haven't touched anything."
runner.notice2: He is already standing when you reach the fire, as though he heard you three rooms back. Sparks drift up past his hood. A spiral is burned into his pack strap. "Same shop," he says.

ui.memoryIntro:
MEMORY

The boss goes still. Something it carried stays behind in all of you: a grip none of you were taught, a way of standing that belongs to someone who came down before.

What you carry out of a fight is held in Memory, run after run. If the whole party falls, what it carried in goes down with it.
